subject: phoenix
pitch: A phoenix rising with its wings flung open. Feathers blaze from deep crimson at the body through orange to golden yellow at the tips, a crest of flame-shaped plumes on its head, long trailing tail feathers like ribbons of fire, glowing amber eyes and a golden hooked beak. Embers and sparks drift off its wings.
reasoning:
I'm thinking through how to position the phoenix model so it reads as rising in flight while keeping its lowest points, like the tail feathers, just above ground level.

Now I'm sketching the skeleton: a root joint at the body center, with spine chains running from pelvis to chest to neck to head, plus wing chains, tail feather joints, and tucked legs. I'm planning the body as a sweep along the spine chain with a gradient paint from deep crimson to orange, then adding a neck chain up to the head with beak cones, a jaw joint, and amber emissive eyes.

For the wings, I'm defining a shoulder-to-wingtip chain on each side with raised, outward-flung geometry, swept as a tube, and adding flight feathers as extruded leaf-shaped parts attached along the wing bones. I'm colouring these feathers with a gradient that shifts from crimson near the body to gold at the wingtips, using a mix function based on distance from center.

I'm working out the local coordinate frame for each feather -- choosing the width axis toward the wingtip and the length axis pointing backward, then computing the cross product to get the correct surface normal pointing upward, with a slight droop added to the length direction for a natural feather curve.

I'm sketching an asymmetric flame-like outline for each feather using a handful of points along the width and length, letting the extrusion auto-orient without worrying about smoothing since blocky edges are cheap to render. Rough triangle budget comes out to around 54 points per wing plus tail feathers, which should stay well under the limit.

Now I'm working out how feathers attach to the wing skeleton: primaries bind to the hand joint, secondaries to the elbow/wrist, referenced by bone name. I'm laying out the wing as a path from shoulder to elbow to wrist to tip, placing secondaries along the elbow-wrist segment with growing lengths swept backward, primaries fanning out along wrist-to-tip with larger lengths, shorter tertials near the shoulder, and coverts as short rows layered on top for natural coloring.

For color, I want it to depend on distance from the body center so wingtips and tail ends gleam gold while the base stays crimson -- computing a distance metric from the torso and mapping it to color stops: crimson near the body, red further out, orange beyond that, and amber gold at the extremities.

I'll add subtle noise variation to the gradient so feathers don't look flat, and layer each primary feather with a smaller bright yellow inner feather lifted slightly above it for extra richness and a flame-like effect, applying this doubling to both primaries and tail feathers.

For the body, I'm defining a curved spine chain with a tapering radius function that's widest in the middle and rounds at both ends, then adding a glowing orange-gold breast patch as a scaled sphere at the chest.

For the neck and head, I'm building a three-point chain that sweeps from the chest up to the head joint, with a tapering radius, then placing a sphere at the head position with the beak to follow as a rotated cone shape.

Now I'm shaping the upper beak as a cone with a hooked tip, adding a smaller angled jaw cone beneath it as its own joint with darker gold coloring, then placing amber eye spheres with dark pupils and a small brow flame detail.

Next I'm building the head crest as five fanned flame-plume feathers extruding up and back with varied lengths and lateral tilts, then starting on the tail as seven long ribbon-feather chains.

Shaping the width profile and tip caps...

Still working out feather curve coordinates...

Adding a thinner inner-highlight sweep offset slightly upward for depth. Now sketching leg chains for tucked talons with hip, knee, ankle, and toe-tip joints positioned to mirror left and right sides.

Still defining wing chain joints...

Still working out feather geometry...

I'm planning two rows of covert feathers along the arm and primaries, positioning them slightly forward and elevated to cover the feather bases, then defining a reusable feather generator function that extrudes an outline shape with configurable position, direction, length, width, and color.

I'm tuning the thickness taper and smoothing settings to get a tapered, slightly curved flame-like feather shape, estimating triangle counts to confirm roughly 150 feathers stay performant, and considering making the tips asymmetric and curled for a more dynamic silhouette.

For coloring, I'm planning to reuse a single fire gradient paint across feathers, but add a lighter inner overlay (smaller, lifted slightly off the surface) for primaries, tail, and crest feathers, using a shifted version of the same gradient function to create variation without duplicating logic. Writing gradient stop definitions...

Tweaking the distance weighting so wingtips reach gold while secondaries stay red-orange and the body/head remain crimson toward the center.

Now I'm thinking through the body shading with a slight countershading offset, a gold-orange chest patch, and then planning a scattering of 40 small ember shapes around the wings using randomized positions, scales, and warm color variation.

Embers should attach near the root joint rather than individual bones, so I'm setting up a single root joint at the base of the spine with the spine chain parented to it, keeping the coordinate convention that left is +X and forward is +Z. I'll skip adding neck ruffs or chest feather tufts for simplicity, focusing instead on the head crest plumes.

Still working out plume geometry...

Tallying feather counts: tertials, secondaries, primaries, coverts per wing doubled, plus tail sweeps and crest plumes, adding small y-offsets to prevent primary feathers from z-fighting since they're nearly coplanar. Now starting to write the actual Three.js build code.

Writing fire gradient function...

Adding jaw joint, beak cone, and hook geometry...

Adding toe cones for each foot and checking overall proportions so the lowest points like the tail rest near ground level while legs and wings stay within a sensible height range.

For the tail chain, I'm setting up joint naming and a sweep path that curves slightly with a sine wave offset, computing a tapering radius along its length -- but I need to fix the sine calculation since it goes negative near the tip, so I'll clamp the parameter range to avoid that.

Still writing sweep logic...

Still building the wing chain and feather fan logic...

Still working out the inner feather offsets...

I'm tapering each feather's thickness so it's wide at the base and thin at the tip, then staggering layers with incremental lift so they visibly separate. Now I'm defining the three wing feather groups—tertials, secondaries, and primaries—each as a fan with its own angle range, length, width, and bone attachment point.

Still working out primary lengths...

Adding ember particles now, scattering octahedron shapes below the wings with random sizes, colors, and rotations for a drifting fire effect.
